newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-JONES STRETCHES LEAD AT TUCSON CLASSIC TO THREE STROKES.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-JONES STRETCHES LEAD AT TUCSON CLASSIC TO THREE STROKES.

text.p: Steve Jones shot a four-under-par 68 to extend his second-round lead at the Tucson Classic to three strokes on Friday.
Jones was at 10-under 134, followed by three golfers including Paul Stankowski, last week's winner in Hawaii.
Stankowski, who shot a 65, was joined at seven under by Kirk Triplett and Brad Bryant, both of whom shot 69.
Jones's first-round co-leader, Jeff Maggert, was alone at six under after a 72.
Jones had a bogey-free day, with three of his four birdies coming on the par fives.

"The par fives have saved me both days. I've birdied seven of the eight, which is good because the par threes have been giving me problems. I think I've only hit two of those greens in regulation," said Jones.
Jones won the Phoenix Open wire to wire last month, with an ultimate victory margin of 11 strokes, but said that the lead he has opened up this week is quite different.
"I was 16 under after two rounds there, so I'm six back of what I shot in that tournament. But if I had putted well this week, I'd be right up there.

"But I'm really pleased with my ball striking, and I'm going to try to continue hitting it that well. Anytime you lead a tournament, you have to get in the mindset that if you're going to lose, lose it being aggressive."

Jones's opening round of 66 was played in a stiff wind, but Friday's conditions were calm. Stankowski, whose score improved seven shots from Thursday to Friday, said that except for the wind, he played just as well both days.
After a practice round on Tuesday Triplett had predicted that the PGA Tour's 27-under-par scoring record was in jeopardy.
"The greens were soft at the start of the week, and there's no rough. I figured six under would be the cut. Here I am at seven under, and I'm in second place," said Triplett.
One of the other players in second place, Bryant, said that the tournament could easily wind up being just a contest for second place.

"Steve Jones has to stumble. If he plays great, no one is going to catch him, because I don't think there is anyone out here this week who can out-putt him," said Bryant. "I've always thought that Steve was one of the best players to ever wear cleats, his only problem is consistency."
